summary: The generated-census rebuild is real and it holds where it was measured. All thirteen frozen versions of this lineage on disk are pinned with their verdict files at digests that match live bytes; all fifty-nine reviewer finding identifiers discoverable on disk are disposed; basedOn.predecessorPinningShape is true at every one of the thirteen objects it describes, including the gradeRuling clause that killed v13; the twelve join currencies are correct under both heading spellings and each join's subject and verdict digests really do appear in its own COORD entry; the fourteen classes' leftoverDesign assertions all match the named joins' live bytes; classEqualityAssertion HOLDS under canonical JSON comparison; siteCount 46 equals the sum of sitesByReason and equals the sites I counted; and the doesNot union is exactly the twenty-member union of the twelve current joins. What fails is the seam where hand-written text was carried past the generator. Two dispositions assert repairs the bytes do not show: CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-1 says the do-not-record enumeration now names every unrecorded frozen version when doesNot[13] is unchanged and names three, two of them recorded; and PPBSV13-B4 with CLAUDE-PPBS-V12-ADV-4 say basedOn.relation's broad claim was replaced when 'and changes nothing else' survives verbatim in a field whose next sentence enumerates three further additions. Two generated counts are wrong against the bytes they count: predecessorV5.role says three Stage A identifiers where two exist anywhere on disk, and findingDisposition emits the entire thirteen-entry v13 block twice, 74 entries for 61 distinct identifiers.

The thirteen entries whose source is 'preview-product-boundary-successor.v13 Stage A' appear at indices 39 through 51 and again, byte-identical in every member, at indices 60 through 72. Each duplicated pair is identical under canonical JSON comparison, so this is a repeated emission of one block, not two dispositions of one identifier. The duplicated identifiers are CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-B1, CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-B2, CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-SF1, CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-1, CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-2, CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-3, CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-4, PPBSV13-B1, PPBSV13-B2, PPBSV13-B3, PPBSV13-B4, PPBSV13-S1 and PPBSV13-S2 — precisely the thirteen findings this subject exists to land.
blockers.whyItMatters: The dispatch stakes this subject on a generator: 'Every Stage A finding identifier discoverable on disk across the lineage (fifty-nine) is disposed, and the generator aborts if any is missing or carries empty disposition text.' PPBSV13-B2's own disposition repeats that abort clause as its landing. A generator that emits the same thirteen-entry block twice ran the v13 stage twice and detected neither pass, which means the closure property the file advertises was not enforced over the array it produced — the abort guard tests for absence and empty text and evidently not for the array it wrote. It is also the one array a later SATISFIED-GRADE cycle would count: counted as entries it reports 74 and 61 in the same breath, and the thirteen findings under review are exactly the thirteen double-counted.

advisories.observation: Fifty-one of the seventy-four entries carry "severity": "LANDED". LANDED is a disposition state, not a severity, and it overwrites the grade the raising reviewer gave: PPBSV13-B1 (MUST-FIX), PPBSV13-S1 (SHOULD-FIX) and CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-1 (ADVISORY) are indistinguishable in this array. The twenty-one carried entries above them do keep BLOCKER, SHOULD-FIX and ADVISORY, so the array uses the member two ways. Nothing is false and preview-product-boundary-successor.v13 did the same, so this is not a bar; a separate disposition member would let the severities survive the landing.

The carried dispositions' landedAt arrays point at field paths as preview-product-boundary-successor.v10 held them. CLAUDE-PPBS-V9-SF1 says it landed at basedOn.predecessorV8.role and joinCurrencyAudit.standing because those two fields named the D-293 Decision 5 limbs and listed what that successor added; I verified both against frozen preview-product-boundary-successor.v10 and the claim is true there. In preview-product-boundary-successor.v14 the census rewrote basedOn.predecessorV8.role to the uniform role sentence and joinCurrencyAudit.standing to the four-superseded measurement, and neither now carries the described content. PPBS-V14-CARRIED-STANDING scopes the carried block correctly and warns that a named leftover-join version is the one current at preview-product-boundary-successor.v10's dispatch; it does not say the same of landedAt field pointers. One clause would close it.

predecessorStanding carries a standing member for v1, v2, v3, v4, v6, v7, v9, v11, v12 and v13 and none for v5, v8 or v10. The three absences are covered — v10 in currentBeforeThisFileIsRecorded, v5 in earlierStanding, v8 in its basedOn role sentence and nowhere else in this section — so nothing is missing from the record. In a rebuild whose whole method is uniformity, the one section left uneven invites a reader to ask whether v8 was overlooked rather than placed.

gradeRuling.question: D-005 form: is preview-product-boundary-successor.v14, as bytes, acceptable at application grade - T2-02's 'application-grade acceptance with no express reservation'?
gradeRuling.reservationSweep: I swept these bytes for anything that would have to travel as an express reservation on an application-grade acceptance and found four defects that are not reservations but blockers, because each is a false statement about the file's own contents rather than a scoped limit on what the file claims. Two dispositions assert repairs the bytes do not carry (CLAUDE-PPBS-V13-ADV-1 on doesNot[13]; PPBSV13-B4 and CLAUDE-PPBS-V12-ADV-4 on basedOn.relation). One generated count is wrong against the identifiers it counts (predecessorV5.role). One generated array double-emits the thirteen findings the subject exists to land (findingDisposition). Beyond those, the sweep is clean and unusually so: I found no unpinned frozen version, no undisposed identifier, no pin-shape clause false at any object, no class assertion the named join does not carry, no stale currency token, no digest that does not match live bytes, no overstatement or understatement of D-316, no deixis, no byte-identity claim, and no SATISFIED, gate-4, gate-5, required-now, G13 or implementation-authorization overreach. The scope limits the file does state - CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, DO-NOT-SEAL, gates 4 and 5 not performed, the D-316 opening not re-performed - are accurate and are the right reservations for a candidate; they are not what defeats the grade.
reasons: A later SATISFIED-GRADE cycle is intended to rest on these bytes, and the four defects sit in exactly the fields such a cycle reads instead of re-walking the directory: the disposition array it would use to confirm the thirteen findings landed, and the relation and role sentences it would use to confirm what changed and what was counted.

Two of the four are the same species this lineage was rejected for three times running - a claim about the predecessor record that the bytes do not satisfy. The generated census genuinely ends that failure inside basedOn, predecessorStanding and recordedInputs, all of which I verified exhaustively; it did not reach doesNot or basedOn.relation, and the dispositions say it did.

The findingDisposition duplication defeats the abort guard the subject advertises as its own proof of closure. The guard tests for a missing identifier and for empty disposition text; it did not test the array it emitted, which carries the v13 block twice.

Application grade with no express reservation requires that a reader who trusts the file's self-description reach the same conclusion as a reader who walks the bytes. On doesNot, on basedOn.relation, on the v5 identifier count and on the disposition array, those two readers diverge.

None of the four is a measurement defect. Every measurement in this subject that I could check against live bytes is correct. The repairs are small and local, and a v15 that makes them should be able to carry every measurement in these bytes forward unchanged.
